svg.aria-label: The private endpoint DNS problem end to end: the public CNAME chain, the two different answers the same name gives depending on who asks, the NXDOMAIN a linked zone creates for everything it does not contain, and the hybrid path with its conditional forwarder trap.
svg.title: One name, two answers, and a zone that is authoritative for everything it does not contain
svg.text: The private endpoint DNS problem, end to end
Creating the endpoint changes nothing about the name. What the name returns depends entirely on which network asked.
1 · THE CHAIN AZURE ADDS, ON PUBLIC DNS
account.blob.core.windows.net
CNAME →
account.privatelink.blob.core.windows.net
This chain is resolvable from anywhere on the internet, deliberately, so hybrid and migrating clients keep working.
2 · THE SAME NAME, TWO ANSWERS
Asked from a VNet linked to the privatelink zone
Azure DNS at 168.63.129.16 answers from the zone
A record → 10.40.40.5 — traffic takes the private endpoint
This is the only vantage point that proves the design works.
Asked from anywhere else
Same chain, followed to the public resolution
Returns the service’s public address, always
A successful lookup here proves nothing about access.
Resource existence is enumerable; resource access is not. The service refuses the connection at its own front door.
3 · LINKING THE ZONE BREAKS EVERYTHING IT DOES NOT CONTAIN
A linked private DNS zone is authoritative for the whole namespace inside that network — including names it has no record for.
Your storage account
Record present in the zone
Resolves → 10.40.40.5
Any other account of the same type
No record in your zone, so no fall-through to public DNS
NXDOMAIN — cached, and the client gets silence
Remedy: ResolutionPolicy = NxDomainRedirect on the virtual network link (API 2024-06-01+). The resolver retries publicly,
using the public endpoint name. It is per link and ships off, so coverage drifts across spokes. A manual A record holding
the public IP also works and is documented as not recommended — it will not track a changing public address.
4 · ON-PREMISES CANNOT ASK AZURE DNS DIRECTLY
On-premises DNS server
conditional forwarder
Forwarder or Private Resolver
inside a VNet linked to the zone
answers from the linked private zone
Queries for private endpoints must originate from the linked virtual network. The forwarder proxies on their behalf; that is
its purpose, not a performance choice. 168.63.129.16 is a host-node virtual IP: no UDRs apply, and it has no reverse lookup.
The forwarder targets the PUBLIC zone name — database.windows.net, never privatelink.database.windows.net
Clients ask for the public name. Forward only the privatelink name and the CNAME is never followed, so nothing uses it.
Three traps here share one shape: a wrong zone name, a privatelink forwarder, a shared zone. None of them returns an error.
